chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿĀṣimī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There was a woman in al-Madīnah to whom men used to come. That reached ʿUmar, so he sent for her, frightened her, and ordered that she be brought to him. The woman became terrified, labor pains seized her, and she went off to one of the houses and gave birth to a boy. The boy cried out at birth, then died. Because of the woman’s terror and the death of the boy, distress entered upon him. Some of those sitting with him said to him, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, there is nothing upon you in this.” And some of them said, “What is this?” He said, “Ask Abā al-Ḥasan.” So Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said to them: “If you exercised ijtihad, then you were not correct; and if you spoke by your own opinion, you have certainly erred.”
Then he said: “The blood-money of the child is upon you.”

key_terms.اجْتَهَدْتُمْ: You exerted legal reasoning or judgment.
key_terms.بِرَأْيِكُمْ: By your own opinion or personal judgment.
key_terms.دِيَةُ: Blood-money; financial compensation due for wrongful death.
key_terms.فَاسْتَهَلَّ: He cried out at birth, indicating live birth.

ai.seo_question: Who is liable if fright or coercion causes a woman to miscarry or lose her child in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report recounts a case in which a woman was terrified by an official summons, went into labor, and the child later died. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام ruled that liability remained for the child's blood-money, establishing a legal judgment tied to harm caused through intimidation and wrongful action.
